p: The ad presents Artifact Share, showing how users can leave inline comments on AI-generated spec documents, have a CLI AI agent read comments and apply changes, and update the document under the same URL.
Artifact Share lets teams review and comment directly on AI-generated docs, allowing coding agents to consume feedback and republish updates to the same link.

[{"timestamp":"00:00","observation":"Hook displays text query asking who reviews agent-written specs over a scrolling background."},{"timestamp":"00:05","observation":"Inline text highlighting and comment box interaction demonstration."},{"timestamp":"00:12","observation":"Terminal CLI view showing Claude command processing the comment."},{"timestamp":"00:17","observation":"Updated spec page reflects 3-week timeline cut with resolved comment thread."}]

The pacing clearly walks through the feedback loop from UI comment to CLI agent execution and republication. Legibility holds up well at mobile feed sizes. Visual transitions between terminal and web doc are clean and functional.

p: ["hook is a static doc screenshot, not motion-driven despite 'live-motion hook bg' concept","generic decision-doc UI may not instantly read as 'agent-authored' without reading captions","CTA button text appears low-contrast/washed out in final frame vs promised 'high-contrast CTA'"]

The narrative arc (spec → human comment → agent edit via CLI → republished doc → CTA) is clear and well-sequenced, directly demonstrating the product's core loop rather than just implying it. Terminal frame showing 'claude -p' and multi-agent support (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) is a strong, specific trust signal for the target dev audience. Weaknesses: the opening frame is a static webpage screenshot with no visible motion or human presence, which undercuts the promised 'hook' and may not stop a scroll in the first second; the final CTA button looks pale gray rather than high-contrast, weakening click intent versus the stated design goal.
